smartcity-api's boot runs migrations and resets user passwords against the SHARED production Neon database. Standing it up is not side-effect-free with respect to production data, even though it serves no traffic.
node's fetch on this host does not trust the TLS-interception CA. Use curl, or set NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca. This silently broke two separate instruments before it was diagnosed.

A CRLF stash from a Windows checkout can be load-bearing: GCP serves dashboards' static assets WITH CRLF, so 'tidying' line endings to LF introduced a real 5-endpoint divergence. Do not normalize a build context for cosmetics.

The api container will report (unhealthy) to Docker. THIS IS NOT A SERVICE PROBLEM. Dockerfile.api's HEALTHCHECK calls curl, which node:22-slim does not ship, so every probe fails with 'curl: not found' while the app answers /api/health with status ok and db connected. It was invisible on GCP because Cloud Run ignores the Docker HEALTHCHECK. On plain Docker it is cosmetic (an unhealthy-but-running container is not restarted). But DO APP PLATFORM DOES HONOUR HEALTHCHECK — so before moving this image to App Platform, fix the probe (install curl, or use a node-based check). Otherwise the platform will mark a correctly-working service unhealthy, and it will look like the migration broke the app.

LESSON: A Cloud Run image deployed by digest records its commit nowhere. Correlate the revision creation time and the build-source zip timestamp against git commit times, then CONFIRM with a blob-hash probe of the actual build context using sed to strip CR before hashing.

When a service depends on an outbound third-party fetch, a new host's EGRESS IP is part of the deployment and must be validated. Use a second host in the same account and region as the control — it separates 'the site blocks DigitalOcean' from 'the site blocks this address'.
Swap does not raise a V8 heap ceiling. Node sizes old-space from VISIBLE memory, so a build that OOMs at ~475MB on a 1GB host needs NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size, not more swap.
docker --env-file folds a stray CR into every value, so LF-verify env files first — otherwise the failure looks like a wrong credential.
An app that defaults to process.env.PORT || 5000 needs PORT set explicitly off Cloud Run; Cloud Run injects it invisibly, so it appears in no env listing.
Exporting a file through a PowerShell variable is not byte-safe — it destroyed newlines and produced a one-line Dockerfile. scp and `git -c core.autocrlf=false archive` are byte-exact.

A Docker HEALTHCHECK that calls curl silently fails on any `slim` base image, because slim variants omit curl. It is invisible on Cloud Run (which ignores Docker HEALTHCHECK) and visible the moment the image runs anywhere that honours it — so a health flag reading 'unhealthy' next to a 200 on the health endpoint means check the probe binary before believing the flag.
